title: Core Variables v4.0
content_markdown: OpenSIPS provides multiple type of variables to be used in the routing script. The difference between the types of variables comes from (1) the visibility of the variable (when it is visible), (2) what the variable is attached to (where the variable resides), (3) read-write status of the variable (some types of the variables are read-only and (4) how multiple values (for the same variable are handled). The OpenSIPS variables can be easily identified in the script as all their names (or notations) start with the $ sign.

variables.name: $var(name)
variables.description: Script variables strictly bound to the script routes. Visible only in the routing blocks, process related. Inherited by script routes executed by the same OpenSIPS process.

variables.name: $avp(name)
variables.description: Attribute Value Pair. Dynamic variables linked to a singular message or transaction. Visible in all routes where any message of the transaction will be processed.

variables.name: $ai
variables.description: reference to URI in request's P-Asserted-Identity header (see RFC 3325)

variables.name: $adu
variables.description: URI from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header. This URI is used when calculating the HTTP Digest Response.

variables.name: $ar
variables.description: realm from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $au
variables.description: user part of username from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $ad
variables.description: domain part of username from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $an
variables.description: the nonce from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.resp
variables.description: the authentication response from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.nonce
variables.description: the nonce string from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.opaque
variables.description: the opaque string from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.alg
variables.description: the algorithm string from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.qop
variables.description: the value of qop parameter from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $auth.nc
variables.description: the value of nonce count parameter from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $aU
variables.description: whole username from Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header

variables.name: $Au
variables.description: username for accounting purposes. It's a selective pseudo variable (inherited from acc module). It returns $au if exits or From username otherwise.

variables.name: $argv
variables.description: provides access to command line arguments specified with '-o' option.

examples.code:
# for option '-o foo=0'
xlog("foo is $argv(foo) \n");

variables.name: $bf
variables.description: displays a list with the branch flags set for the current SIP request. TO BECOME OBSOLETE, replaced by $msg.branch.flags

variables.name: $branch
variables.description: this variable is used for creating new branches by writing into it the value of a SIP URI. TO BECOME OBSOLETE, replaced by $msg.branch.uri

variables.name: $branch()
variables.description: this variable provides read/write access to all fields/attributes of an already existing branch. TO BECOME OBSOLETE, replaced by $msg.branch.uri

subfields.name: uri
subfields.description: the RURI of the branch

subfields.name: duri
subfields.description: destination URI of the branch (outbound proxy of the branch)

subfields.name: q
subfields.description: q value of the branch

subfields.name: path
subfields.description: the PATH string for this branch

subfields.name: flags
subfields.description: the branch flags of this branch

subfields.name: socket
subfields.description: the local socket to be used for relaying this branch

variables.name: $branch.flag()
variables.description: this variable provides read/write access to the value of a single certain branch flag (identified by name). TO BECOME OBSOLETE, replaced by $msg.branch.flag

variables.name: $challenge.algorithm
variables.description: the algorithm value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

variables.name: $challenge.realm
variables.description: the realm value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

variables.name: $challenge.nonce
variables.description: the nonce value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

variables.name: $challenge.opaque
variables.description: the opaque value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

variables.name: $challenge.qop
variables.description: the qop value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

variables.name: $challenge.ik
variables.description: the ik value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

variables.name: $challenge.ck
variables.description: the ck value taken from the WWW-Authorize or Proxy-Authorize header.

variables.name: $ci
variables.description: reference to body of call-id header

variables.name: $cl

variables.name: $cs
variables.description: reference to cseq number from cseq header

variables.name: $ct
variables.description: reference to contact instance/body from the contact header.

variables.name: $ct.fields()
variables.description: reference to the fields of a contact instance/body.

examples.code:
$ct.fields(uri)
$(ct.fields(name)[1])

subfields.description: display name

subfields.name: uri

subfields.name: methods

subfields.name: received

subfields.name: params

variables.description: reference to body of Content-Type header and also the content-type headers inside a multi-part body

variables.name: $dd

variables.name: $du

variables.name: $err.class
variables.description: the class of error (now is '1' for parsing errors)

variables.name: $err.rcode

variables.name: $fd

variables.name: $fn
variables.description: reference to display name of 'From' header

variables.name: $ft
variables.description: reference to tag parameter of 'From' header

variables.name: $fu

variables.name: $fU

variables.name: $log_level
variables.description: changes the log level for the current process

variables.name: $mb
variables.description: reference to SIP message buffer

variables.name: $mf
variables.description: displays a list with the message/transaction flags set for the current SIP request

variables.name: $mi
variables.description: reference to SIP message id

variables.name: $ml
variables.description: reference to SIP message length

variables.name: $msg.branch
variables.description: similar to $branch, this variable is used for creating new message branches by writing into it the value of a SIP URI.

variables.name: $msg.branch.uri
variables.description: gives read / write access over the SIP URI (as string) of an existing message branch.

examples.code:
# creates a new branch
$msg.branch = "sip:new@domain.org";
# change its URI
$msg.branch.uri = "sip:new_new@domain.org"
# change its URI of RURI branch
$(msg.branch.uri[0]) = "sip:new_RURI@domain.org"

variables.name: $msg.branch.duri
variables.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with the Detination-URI value of the message branch.

variables.name: $msg.branch.path
variables.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with the PATH value of the message branch.

variables.name: $msg.branch.q
variables.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with the Q value of the message branch.

variables.name: $msg.branch.flags
variables.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with list (comma separated) of per-branch flags (which are set for the branch).

variables.name: $msg.branch.socket
variables.description: 100% similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating with the (forced) socket value of the message branch.

variables.name: $msg.branch.flag()
variables.description: similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating over a single branch flag (for the current branch).

variables.name: $msg.branch.attr()
variables.description: similar to $msg.branch.uri, but operating over a single branch attribute (attached to the current branch).

variables.name: $msg.branch.last_idx
variables.description: returns the index of the last message branch.

variables.name: $msg.flag()
variables.description: this variable provides read/write access to the value of a single certain message flag (identified by name).

variables.name: $msg.is_request
variables.description: this variable tells if the current SIP message is a request or not.

variables.name: $msg.type
variables.description: this variable returns the type of the current message. The returned values are "request" (request) or "reply" (reply).

examples.code: xlog("---- this message is a SIP $msg.type \n");

variables.name: $op

variables.name: $param()
variables.description: retrieves the parameters of the route. The index can be an integer, or a pseudo-variable (index starts at 1).

variables.name: $pd
variables.description: reference to domain in request's P-Preferred-Identity header URI (see RFC 3325)

variables.name: $proxy_protocol()
variables.description: retrieves Proxy Protocol information from the transport layer.

variables.name: $sdp
variables.description: Read/Write reference to the SDP body of the current SIP message

examples.code:
# READ operation on the SIP msg SDP
$sdp

# WRITE operation (assign a new SDP)
$sdp = $var(rtpengine_sdp);

# READ operation on the SIP reply SDP
$(<reply>sdp)

# WRITE operation (assign a new SDP to SIP reply)
$(<reply>sdp) = $var(rtpengine_sdp);

variables.name: $sdp.line
variables.description: Read/Write reference to SDP body lines, with filtering support

examples.code:
# Fetch the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc. attribute line (starting with "a=")
$sdp.line(a=)         # fetch first "a=" lin
$sdp.line(a=[0])      # equivalent, "a=" line at index 0
$sdp.line(a=ptime[1]) # "a=ptime" line at index 1
$sdp.line(a=[100])    # will likely yield NULL

# Token-based filtering, inside a line
$sdp.line(m=audio[1])         # m=audio 27292 RTP/AVP 9 8 0 2 102 100 99 101
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/[0])     # audio
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/[1])     # 27292
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/[2])     # RTP/AVP
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/[10])    # 101
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/[11])    # NULL
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/RTP)         # RTP/AVP
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/RTP\/AVP)    # RTP/AVP
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/RTP\/AVP[0]) # RTP/AVP
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/RTP\/AVP[1]) # NULL
$sdp.line(m=audio[1]/RTQ)         # NULL

variables.name: $sdp.stream
variables.description: Read/Write reference to SDP body streams, with filtering support

examples.code:
# Within a desired stream, you can first filter by line...
$sdp.stream(/a=ptime);         # first a=ptime line from Stream #0 ("m=", matching any stream type)
$sdp.stream([1]/a=ptime);      # first a=ptime line from Stream #1 ("m=", matching any stream type))
$sdp.stream(audio[1]/a=ptime); # first a=ptime line from Audio Stream #1 ("m=audio...")
$sdp.stream(a[1]/a=ptime);     # first a=ptime line from Audio Stream #1 ("m=a...")
$sdp.stream(video[1]/a=nortpproxy) = NULL;  # delete entire line starting with "a=nortpproxy" from Video Stream #1
$sdp.stream(v[1]/a=nortpproxy:/[0]) = yes;   # set first "a=nortpproxy" line "yes" value, in Video Stream #1

# ... and, additionally, by token
$sdp.stream(video[1]/a=fmtp:115/bitrate=) = 48000; # set "bitrate=" to 48000, under "a=fmtp:115" line #0, as part of Video Stream #1
$sdp.stream(video[1]/a=fmtp:115[3]) = NULL; # delete the 4th occurrence (if any) of "a=fmtp:115" line, but only within Video Stream #1
$sdp.stream(video[1]/a=fmtp:115/bitrate=) = 48000; # set "bitrate=" to 48000, under "a=fmtp:115" line #0, as part of Video Stream #1

variables.name: $sdp.session
variables.description: Read/Write reference to the SDP body session, with filtering support

examples.code:
# Within the SDP session (i.e. until the 1st "m=" line), you can first filter by line...
$sdp.session(a=ptime);            # 1st a=ptime line at Session level
$sdp.session(a=ptime[0]);         # same as above
$sdp.session(a=ptime[1]);         # 2nd a=ptime line at Session level
$sdp.session(a=ptime[0]) = NULL;  # delete 1st a=ptime line at Session level

# ... but also filter and edit by token:
$sdp.session(a=rtpmap/telephone-event\/) = "8000";  # Match 1st "a=rtpmap" line which describes telephone-event at Session level, and force bitrate to 8000

variables.name: $sdp.stream.idx
variables.description: Read-Only reference to the index of the matched SDP stream. Yields NULL on no-match.

examples.code:
$var(line_idx) = $sdp.stream.idx(video/a=fmtp/packetization-mode=); # locate index of first "a=fmtp" line, containing a packetization-mode= attribute
$var(data) = $sdp.line([$var(line_idx)]); # grab the full line data
... perform processing on that line ...
$sdp.line([$var(line_idx)]) = $var(data); # re-write the line

variables.name: $si
variables.description: reference to IP source address of the message

variables.name: $socket_in
variables.description: read-only variable to get the description (proto:ip:port format) of the inbound socket (used for receiving the message).

subfields.name: ip
subfields.description: the IP part of the socket

subfields.name: port
subfields.description: the port part of the socket

subfields.name: proto
subfields.description: the name of the protocol of the socket

subfields.name: advertised_ip
subfields.description: the advertised IP part of the socket

subfields.name: advertised_port
subfields.description: the advertised part part of the socket

subfields.name: tag
subfields.description: the socket internal tag/alias

subfields.name: anycast
subfields.description: if the socket uses an anycast IP or not

subfields.name: af
subfields.description: the address family of the socket's IP

variables.name: $socket_out
variables.description: read-write variable for reading or changing the outbound socket of the message.

examples.code:
$socket_out = "udp:11.11.11.11:5060";
xlog("The outbound port is $socket_out(port)\n");

subfields.name: ip
subfields.description: the IP part of the socket

subfields.name: port
subfields.description: the port part of the socket

subfields.name: proto
subfields.description: the name of the protocol of the socket

subfields.name: advertised_ip
subfields.description: the advertised IP part of the socket

subfields.name: advertised_port
subfields.description: the advertised part part of the socket

subfields.name: tag
subfields.description: the socket internal tag/alias

subfields.name: anycast
subfields.description: if the socket uses an anycast IP or not

subfields.name: af
subfields.description: the address family of the socket's IP

subfields.name: forced
subfields.description: returns a socket description only if a socket had been explicitly forced

variables.name: $td

variables.name: $time()
variables.description: returns the string formatted time according to UNIX date

variables.name: $T_branch_idx
variables.description: the index (starting with 1 for the first branch) of the branch for which is executed the branch_route[].

variables.name: $Tf
variables.description: reference string formatted time

variables.name: $Ts
variables.description: reference to current unix time stamp in seconds

variables.name: $Tsm
variables.description: reference to current microseconds of the current second

variables.name: $TS
variables.description: reference to startup unix time stamp

variables.name: $ua

variables.name: $hdr()
variables.description: represents the body of the N-th header identified by 'name'.

variables.name: $route
variables.description: Access route names of the current route call stack.

variables.name: $route.type
variables.description: Access the type of the current route. May be indexed, using positive or negative indexes.

variables.name: $route.name
variables.description: Access the name of the current route. May be indexed, using positive or negative indexes.

variables.name: $cfg_line
variables.description: Holds the current line from the script of the action being executed, useful for logging purposes

variables.name: $cfg_file
variables.description: Holds the current name of the cfg file being executed, useful when using multiple scripts via the include statement

variables.name: $xlog_level
variables.description: allows to set /reset the xlog() logging level on per-process bases.

examples.code:
xlog("current verbosity is $xlog_level \n");
$xlog_level = L_DBG; # force local xlogging limit to DBG
...
(set of xlogs)
...
$xlog_level = NULL;  # reset to initial value

variables.name: $C()
variables.description: reference to an escape sequence. x represents the foreground color and y represents the background color.
